transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Time: 15:00-15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Lighthouse CTO), Sara Kim (ML Eng), Omar Reyes (Infra), Nina (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Reviewed tokens/sec per dollar metrics, saw caching giving 28-42% cost savings depending on workload patterns.
- Batch size tradeoffs discussed: latency vs tokens/sec/$ with concrete examples.
- Agreed on tests: KV hit pattern runs, batch sweep, and a VPC options demo next week.

Topics: cost/unit economics, caching savings, batching tradeoffs, latency SLOs, private deployment constraints

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we have a full set today, i'll kick off, quick agenda: recap last weeks numbers, dig into caching numbers, batching sweep, and then next steps.
[00:18] Daniel: thanks Maya, quick FYI we've got execs asking about "tokens per dollar" and need a clear chart for monday, so hoping to get the numbers today.
[00:34] Maya: yep understood, we'll try to make the math concrete. Liam, you wanna start with the raw pilot results?
[00:39] Liam: sure, uh quick caveat first, some of the earlier runs had the replica config slightly off so we re-run the baseline yesterday, baseline means warm KV disabled, batch size 1, hosted model redwood-llama-v2-13b-quant (note: transcript might show model name garbled). Baseline tokens per dollar for that setup was ~2,100 tokens/$ at p50 latency ~120ms.
[01:05] Sara: that baseline sounds about right compared to our earlier microbenchmarks, we typically see long prompts so baseline is a bit lower.
[01:20] Liam: ok then we enabled KV prefix cache and hit ratio varied by test: 35% hit -> tokens/$ jumped to ~2,900 (roughly +38%), 60% hit -> tokens/$ to ~3,400 (+62% vs baseline) but p95 latency increased slightly in high batch runs.
[01:45] Omar: can you explain hit ratio again, we saw different numbers in our trace, is that because of prefix length?
[01:52] Liam: yeah it's a combo: prefix length, prompt reuse across sessions, and the caching window. for us the test sim used repeated user prompts typical of retail chat flows so hit ratio was optimistic, real world might be lower.
[02:10] [02:10] Daniel: uh hm, our real logs show more ad hoc prompts, reuse maybe 10-15% not 35-60. so i want to see both scenarios.
[02:22] Maya: good call. we'll produce conservative & optimistic columns in the spreadsheet.
[02:28] Liam: next batching: we swept batch sizes 1,4,8,16. tokens/sec/$ improved up to batch=8, beyond that returns diminished and latencies start to climb. numbers: batch=1 -> 2,100 tokens/$, batch=4 -> 2,700, batch=8 -> 3,300, batch=16 -> 3,400 but p95 latency doubled from 120ms to ~250ms at 16.
[03:00] Sara: that aligns with our concerns, latency-sensitive flows hit p95 limits at batch 16. our threshold is p95 < 200ms for checkout chat.
[03:15] Liam: right, so tradeoff: to get higher tokens/$ you can push batching and caching, but you hit latency SLOs. Redwood runtime can do dynamic routing though - route latency-sensitive reqs to lower-batch pools.
[03:30] Maya: question for Lighthouse: what's more important, raw tokens/$ or keeping latency SLAs for the 10% high-priority flows?
[03:40] Daniel: we need to preserve SLAs for checkout and fraud detection chat. so i'd say keep p95 < 200ms for those lanes, everything else can be opportunistically batched.
[03:52] Maya: perfect — that's actionable.
[04:00] [04:00] Omar: also want to bring up network jitter when peering across clouds, we've seen spikes that blow p95 out, is there a way to mitigate?
[04:10] Liam: yes, that's where dedicated or private deployment helps. with Redwood Dedicated you get reserved pools in the same region and predictable networking, less jitter. if you need air-gapped, Redwood Private gives on-prem option but pricing/ops differ.
[04:30] Nina: quick Q, we heard about "auto-coldstart" mitigation - is that the prefix cache?
[04:35] Liam: it's one piece; we also do kernel warmup and preloading for common prompt shapes, and continuous batching to reduce cold starts. transcript sometimes garbles 'kernel' as 'canal' so ignore that.
[04:50] Sara: can you show the delta for cost when we enable both caching and batching? aggregate number?
[04:56] Liam: yes, combined conservative estimate: baseline 2,100 -> combined 3,400 tokens/$ (about +62%), optimistic pattern (high reuse) -> up to 4,800 tokens/$. but again those optimistic numbers assumed 60% cache hit and batch=8 consistently which is uncommon for all flows.
[05:20] Daniel: that's a big swing, we need conservative modeling for procurement.
[05:25] Maya: we'll include both and highlight risk.
[05:30] [05:30] Liam: latency profile detail: p50 stays low across batches, p95 is what grows. for batch=8 p95 ~160ms, batch=16 p95 ~250ms. for KV heavy hits p95 can actually drop for repeated prompts because GPU work is smaller.
[05:50] Omar: what about throughput per GPU? tokens/sec numbers?
[05:55] Liam: single GPU peak tokens/sec in our config: baseline ~18k tps, batch=8 -> ~36k tps, with caching we effectively multiply perceived tokens/$ because cached tokens are offloaded, so relative TPS cost goes down.
[06:15] Sara: can we get a worked example for our volume: we expect 1.2M tokens/day with 15% reuse and average seq len 240 tokens.
[06:25] Maya: yes, put that in the sheet and we'll run the worked scenarios.
[06:30] [06:30] Daniel: also curious about model quantization impact on accuracy, you mentioned quantized 13b earlier. any quality regressions we should be worried about?
[06:40] Liam: small bits but we ran evals on your eval set, ROUGE/QA metrics barely moved, still within your guardrails, but we'll share the detailed eval artifacts. note transcript may show model name wrong — it was redwood-llama-13b-int8 test.
[06:58] Maya: action: Liam will upload eval artifacts + diffs to the drive.
[07:05] [07:05] Sara: about routing, you said we can tier requests by intent? how intrusive is that change?
[07:12] Liam: non-intrusive — on the client side you set a route header or tag and send it to route policy. Redwood Console lets you set canary policies, fallback rules — no code change unless you want client-side sampling.
[07:28] Maya: do we need SSO/enterprise setup to demo the private option?
[07:33] Omar: our security team needs SAML + audit logs and KMS integration.
[07:38] Liam: Redwood Private supports SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM for key management, and audit logs. we'll send SOC2/ISO docs but the private option is a licensing + infra install.
[07:52] [07:52] Nina: procurement timeline question: if we sign committed Dedicated capacity, what's the minimum term?
[07:58] Maya: typically monthly with annual discounts for committed capacity; Dedicated contracts often start 90-day ramp, but we can give options. i'll send the exact contract snippets.
[08:10] [08:10] Daniel: ok let's go back to the numbers, can you show a scenario that keeps p95 < 200ms for 10% of traffic but maximizes tokens/$ for the remainder?
[08:20] Liam: yes — hybrid routing: reserve a small low-latency pool (batch=1-2) for high-priority lanes and a pooled high-throughput cluster with batch=8 for the rest. that gives you a blended tokens/$ ~3,200-3,600 depending on cache hit.
[08:40] Sara: what's the incremental cost of reserving that low-latency pool?
[08:45] Maya: depends on size; for example, reserving 2 gpus for low-latency is X dollars/day, the spreadsheet will include per-GPU reserved price and per-token equivalent.
[08:58] [08:58] Omar: any throttling strategies we should consider? spikes during sales events could blow up tokens consumption.
[09:06] Liam: yes rate-limiting, adaptive throttling, and auto-scaling burst pools. Redwood has burst capacity options that tap extra capacity for short windows to avoid dropped requests.
[09:20] Daniel: can we simulate a 10x spike for 10 minutes and get cost delta?
[09:26] Maya: Liam will run that sim and add to sheet.
[09:30] [09:30] Liam: quick note on caching: cache warmup time matters. day-one you'll see lower hit ratios; warmup grows over time, so pilot duration should be at least 7 days to show steady-state savings.
[09:45] Sara: that explains our initial low numbers. good to know.
[09:50] Maya: we'll mark that in the model as "warmup factor".
[09:54] [09:54] Daniel: what about data residency — some customers need EU-only. can Redwood pin regions?
[10:00] Liam: yes region pinning and routing policies exist; for Private deployments you get full control. hosted API also has region options. we'll capture region cost deltas in the spreadsheet.
[10:14] Sara: any known issues with our target cloud (us-west2) for GPU availability?
[10:20] Liam: availability varies — Dedicated gives SLA, hosted best-effort but we can reserve capacity for you under Dedicated.
[10:30] [10:30] Maya: quick break down of the concrete items we'll share: 1) spreadsheet with baseline/conservative/optimistic columns, 2) eval artifacts demonstrating quality delta for quantized models, 3) batch sweep and cache hit test results, 4) contract snippets for Dedicated/Private.
[10:45] Nina: thanks.
[10:48] [10:48] Sara: on the cache tests, can you emulate our prompt distribution specifically — we can export a sample.
[10:52] Liam: please send a 10k prompt sample sanitized and we'll run realistic reuse tests, that will give hit curves.
[10:58] Daniel: timeline to get these numbers? by friday?
[11:02] Maya: we'll aim for Friday EOD(2026-06-11) for initial spreadsheet and tests.
[11:10] [11:10] Omar: about the VPC demo you mentioned, will that require infra time from our side?
[11:16] Liam: minimal — typically a short peering and a small firewall rule change; for full private install we'll need more but demo can be done with limited infra.
[11:30] [11:30] Maya: ok any other blockers?
[11:33] Daniel: procurement wants to understand worst-case monthly cost at 1.5M tokens/day, include 90th percentile token growth.
[11:40] Maya: noted. we'll add a worst-case column.
[11:46] [11:46] Sara: one more question about tooling: can we get token-level tracing to map which prompts generate tokens that get cached later?
[11:52] Liam: yes, Redwood Console has token-level traces and a cache hit dashboard; we'll grant trial console access to your team with read-only perms.
[12:05] [12:05] Maya: recap quick: Liam runs batch+cache tests, share artifacts, Maya shares pricing + contract snippets, customer shares prompt sample and seq length histogram. follow-up demo for private scheduled for week of 6/22.
[12:20] Daniel: good meeting, thanks all.
[12:25] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with the sheet and tests.
[12:30] [12:30] End of transcript (approx). Note: timestamps may drift vs. exact call audio. Some product names and acronyms may be transcribed imperfectly."
